overall: The AG found no OML violation for discussing the Friends' Restated Articles at the June 23 meeting, because the topic naturally flowed from the posted negotiation item. All other allegations were declined as outside OML jurisdiction.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Board discussed the Friends' Restated Articles of Organization at its June 23 meeting, a topic not listed on the notice.
allegations.key_passage: Because we find that the discussion of the Restated Articles of Organization naturally flowed from the discussion of negotiations between the Board and the Friends, we find no violation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged erroneous and unsubstantiated information was presented during the June 23 discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, allegations that the Board or the Library Director presented erroneous information during the discussion, or included purposefully incomplete information in the meeting packet, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the meeting packet deliberately included incomplete and inaccurate documents.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, allegations that the Board or the Library Director presented erroneous information during the discussion, or included purposefully incomplete information in the meeting packet, even if true, would not constitute violations of the Open Meeting Law and we decline to review them.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged a Board member who is an attorney violated duties of competent representation and had a conflict of interest in voting on Friends matters.
allegations.key_passage: Similarly, the Open Meeting Law does not govern the ethical obligations of an attorney, and we therefore decline to review the allegations of conflict of interest and inadequate representation.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the Chair failed to control the meeting and relinquished agenda control to the Library Director, exposing members to liability.
allegations.key_passage: A public body does not violate the Open Meeting Law when it allows a non-member to speak at length, even if his contribution has the effect of steering the body's discussion in a particular direction.
